headline: Hot Springs State Bath House and Dinosaur Dig Bookings
reservation: Access to Hot Springs State Park is generally open, but the State Bath House has specific time-limited entry rules. Specialized 'Dig for a Day' programs at the Dinosaur Center and canyon rafting trips require advance reservations. Check the official Wyoming State Parks site for seasonal pool maintenance closures.

days.title: Ancient Waters and Terraces
days.start: Suggested: 9:30 AM from Hot Springs State Park

stops.name: Big Spring
stops.detail: Witness the source of the mineral water flowing at a constant 135 degrees Fahrenheit.

stops.name: Rainbow Terraces
stops.detail: Walk the boardwalks to see colorful mineral deposits formed by flowing hot water.

days.driving: Minimal; local transfers within the state park area.
days.note: Soaking in the State Bath House is limited to 20 minutes for health reasons.

days.title: Jurassic Giants and Bison Fields

stops.name: Wyoming Dinosaur Center
stops.detail: Tour the museum and active prep lab to see world-class fossil specimens.

stops.name: Bison Pasture Drive
stops.detail: Drive the loop road to observe the state-managed bison herd in their natural habitat.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for local stops; roads are generally well-maintained.
days.note: Bison are unpredictable; remain inside your vehicle at all times.

days.title: Canyons and Ancient Art

stops.name: Wind River Canyon
stops.detail: Drive through the towering rock walls to see spectacular geological formations.

stops.name: Legend Rock State Petroglyph Site
stops.detail: View over 300 prehistoric rock art carvings located 30 miles northwest of town.

days.driving: Allow 2–3 hours round trip; Legend Rock involves rural roads.
days.note: Check the Thermopolis Chamber for access keys or gate codes for Legend Rock.

intel.title: Bath House Congestion
intel.text: Parking at the State Bath House can be competitive on summer weekends. Utilize overflow lots near the Swinging Bridge if the main lot is full.

intel.title: Canyon Dead Zones
intel.text: Signal is lost quickly when driving south into Wind River Canyon. Ensure you have physical directions if traveling toward Riverton or Shoshoni.

intel.title: Basin Logistics
intel.text: Thermopolis is the primary fuel hub for the Bighorn Basin area. Refill your vehicle before heading to remote sites like Legend Rock or Bighorn Canyon.

intel.title: Seasonal Water Flow
intel.text: Rafting in the canyon is typically available from May to September depending on snowpack runoff. Mineral pool steam is most dramatic in the cool morning air.

intel.title: Tribal Land Permits
intel.text: Parts of the Wind River Canyon are on the Wind River Reservation. Stay in designated public pull-outs unless you have a specific tribal fishing or recreation permit.

plan.arrival: Arrive at Central Wyoming Regional (RIW), rent a car, and drive 77 minutes through the canyon to reach Thermopolis lodging.
plan.vehicle: A standard car is fine for town, but an SUV is better for reaching Legend Rock or exploring BLM lands.
plan.goldenHour: Spirit Mountain offers an elevated view of the town and river at sunset, with seasonal variations in light.
